correctness.rationale: Sign change is postcomposition by the diagonal unitary conjugation. PSD of the Hermitian symbol is equivalent to T√(ab)≤1 on the two normalized part means; the other eigenvalues are one. A PSD symbol gives a unital CP map; the strict supercritical lower bound proves noncontractivity, and positivity itself would require a PSD symbol by testing the all-ones positive matrix. For z=2(abT²−1)/D, D=2abT+a+b, the positive difference is zww* and the plus certificate determinant is 4−4abT²+2Dz=0, with positive diagonal. Their CP norms add to 1+z. The stated α,β satisfy aα+bβ=1. Multiplying the witness discriminant by D² reduces the identity to D²=(a−b)²+4ab(bT+1)(aT+1). The two remaining eigenvalues have opposite signs and sum of magnitudes T. Thus the trace norm is 1+T−α−β=1+z, attained on the sign contraction. For two infinite parts, diagonal expectation plus t/2 times the difference of identity and the part-sign conjugation gives a normal cb upper bound 1+T, and increasing balanced finite corners give the ordinary lower bound tending to 1+T. This includes T=0. The frozen rational code was inspected, not executed; these identities prove all dimensions and real weights.
